title: Oats in the Rain
text: The oats are still standing in the low field when the rain comes in from the west.

choices.label: Send everyone to cut them in the rain
choices.chronicle: {When}, the whole house went out in the rain and brought in the oats, wet and cold, and the brothers did not forgive it quickly.

choices.label: Cut the dry strips and leave the rest
choices.chronicle: {When}, the dry strips were cut and the wet oats were left to rot in the field.

title: The Swarm on the Apple Tree
text: The bees have swarmed onto the old apple tree by the wall, and hang there like a brown beard.

choices.label: Hive them in an old straw skep
choices.chronicle: {When}, the swarm was taken into a straw skep, and by autumn the house had a little honey.

choices.label: Let them go over the wall
choices.chronicle: {When}, the swarm went over the wall to the village, and the village kept the bees.

title: Rats in the Granary
text: Rats have got under the granary door in the night and eaten into the corner of the sacks.

choices.label: Set traps and check every sack
choices.chronicle: {When}, the traps were set, and every sack was turned out, and a little was lost to the rats all the same.

choices.label: Move the sacks into the hall
choices.chronicle: {When}, the sacks were carried into the hall in a hurry, and the rats had their share before anyone noticed.

title: The Drip in the Hall
text: Water is coming through the roof of the hall onto the bench where the copyists sit.

choices.label: Send two brothers up with tar and rope
choices.chronicle: {When}, two brothers went up on the roof with tar and rope, and the drip stopped before the feast.

choices.label: Move the bench and wait for fair weather
choices.chronicle: {When}, the bench was moved, and the drip went on for a month in another place.

title: The Missing Key
text: The key of the book cupboard has been missing for three days, and the copyists have started to complain.

choices.label: Search every cell
choices.chronicle: {When}, every cell was searched, and the key was found in the abbot's own sleeve, which no one spoke of.

choices.label: Break the lock and fit a new one
choices.chronicle: {When}, the lock was broken and a new one fitted, and the key that had been lost turned up later in the rushes.

title: Shoes for the Pilgrims
text: Two pilgrims at the gate ask for shoes for the road. The cobbler has leather for one pair only.

choices.label: Give the leather to the pilgrims
choices.chronicle: {When}, the leather went to the pilgrims, who blessed the gate and went on barefoot in their hearts.

choices.label: Keep it for the brothers' feet
choices.chronicle: {When}, the leather was kept for the brothers, and the pilgrims went on down the road without it.

title: Frost on the Blossom
text: A hard frost in the night has taken the blossom from the small orchard.

choices.label: Smoke the orchard with the firewood
choices.chronicle: {When}, the orchard was smoked all night, and a little fruit was saved from the frost.

choices.label: Accept the loss
choices.chronicle: {When}, the blossom was let go, and the autumn was poorer by a few barrels.

title: The Race Overflows
text: The river has come up over the mill race in the night, and the water is in the lower yard.

choices.label: Dig a channel with everyone
choices.chronicle: {When}, the whole house dug a channel by lamplight, and the water went where it was wanted.

choices.label: Let the mill wait for the water to drop
choices.chronicle: {When}, the mill stood idle for a week, and the yard was left to the river.

title: A Letter from the Bishop
text: A letter comes from the bishop asking how many brothers the house can feed through the winter.

choices.label: Answer honestly
choices.chronicle: {When}, the abbot wrote the true number of mouths and the true store, and the bishop answered with a blessing and no more questions.

choices.label: Answer with a larger number
choices.chronicle: {When}, the abbot wrote a larger number than the house had, and the bishop's answer came back with a visitor.

title: A Quarrel at the Desk
text: Two brothers have stopped speaking over the use of the copying desk by the window.

choices.label: Put them to work together in the garden
choices.chronicle: {When}, the two brothers were set to the garden together, and by the end of the month they were arguing about the beans instead.

choices.label: Separate them for a month
choices.chronicle: {When}, the two brothers were kept apart for a month, and the house took sides, quietly.

title: The Taste of Iron
text: The water in the cistern has tasted of iron since the thaw, and the children will not drink it.

choices.label: Drain it and scrub the stone
choices.chronicle: {When}, the cistern was drained and scrubbed, and the water came back sweet within the week.

choices.label: Drink it and hope for the best
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house drank the iron water, and two brothers took the flux, and the medicine went on them.

title: A Visit for the Bees
text: A girl from the village brings a basket of eggs up the hill and asks to see the house's bees.

choices.label: Show her the hives
choices.chronicle: {When}, the girl was shown the hives, and went down the hill with a comb wrapped in a cloth.

choices.label: Send her back to the gate
choices.chronicle: {When}, the girl was sent back to the gate with her eggs, and the village heard of it.

title: The Psalter Is Finished
text: The scribe has finished the psalter a month early, and asks the house to mark the day.

choices.label: Keep a feast for it
choices.chronicle: {When}, a small feast was kept for the finished psalter, and the scribe wept over his bread.

choices.label: Put it on the shelf without fuss
choices.chronicle: {When}, the psalter went on the shelf without fuss, and a copy was ordered for the chapter house.

title: Sheep in the Snow
text: Snow fell hard through the night, and two sheep have been found dead in the glen.

choices.label: Bring the flock down to the sheds
choices.chronicle: {When}, the flock was brought down to the sheds, and the rest of the sheep lived to be shorn.

choices.label: Leave them to the hill
choices.chronicle: {When}, the flock was left on the hill, and the lambs were lost before spring.

title: Wool from a Widow
text: A widow from the village sends a bolt of wool up to the house, unasked.

choices.label: Accept it and send bread back
choices.chronicle: {When}, the wool was accepted, and bread was sent down in return, and the widow's door stayed open.

choices.label: Accept it and say nothing
choices.chronicle: {When}, the wool was taken in quietly, and the widow was not thanked by name.

title: Mice in the Vellum
text: Mice have got into the box of old vellum in the scriptorium loft.

choices.label: Lay out poison
choices.chronicle: {When}, poison was laid out, and the mice died in the loft, and the brothers found it hard to breathe up there for a week.

choices.label: Move the box to the lower store
choices.chronicle: {When}, the box was carried down to the lower store, and the mice were left to the loft.

title: The Flux in the Kitchen
text: The cook's boy has a flux, and it is spreading through the kitchen.

choices.label: Give the cook's boy the medicine
choices.chronicle: {When}, the cook's boy was given the medicine, and the flux went out of the kitchen with him.

choices.label: Close the kitchen for a week
choices.chronicle: {When}, the kitchen was closed for a week, and the bread was late every day of it.

title: Sparks on the Thatch
text: Sparks from the kitchen chimney have caught the thatch of the bake house.

choices.label: Fight it with buckets from the well
choices.chronicle: {When}, the whole house fought the fire with buckets from the well, and the bake house stood, black at the eaves.

choices.label: Let it burn itself out
choices.chronicle: {When}, the fire was let burn, and the bake house was lost to the eaves, and the bread that week was made in the hall.

title: Geese on the Stubble
text: A flock of geese has come down on the stubble in the low field.

choices.label: Drive them off with the boys
choices.chronicle: {When}, the boys drove the geese off, and two were caught in the reeds and brought up for the pot.

choices.label: Let them feed
choices.chronicle: {When}, the geese were let feed, and the field went to them for a week.

title: A Mason on the Road
text: A stonemason passing on the road offers to mend the church wall for bread.

choices.label: Hire him for bread
choices.chronicle: {When}, the mason was given bread for his work, and the church wall stood straight by the autumn.

choices.label: Send him on his way
choices.chronicle: {When}, the mason was sent on, and the wall was propped with timber until spring.

title: The Ox in the Barley
text: The house's ox has broken through the hedge into the neighbour's barley.

choices.label: Pay for the damage
choices.chronicle: {When}, the damage was paid for in grain, and the neighbour sent back a jug of cider.

choices.label: Say the ox is old and wandered
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house said the ox was old and had wandered, and the neighbour did not believe it.

title: The Old Hours
text: The chapter has spent a whole morning arguing whether the bell should still ring at the old hours.

choices.label: Decide for the old hours
choices.chronicle: {When}, the chapter kept the old hours, and the old brothers were glad of it.

choices.label: Decide for the new hours
choices.chronicle: {When}, the chapter chose the new hours, and the old brothers rang the bell themselves at dawn, out of spite.

title: The Latch
text: The gate latch has rusted through, and the gate swings at every wind.

choices.label: Forge a new latch
choices.chronicle: {When}, a new latch was forged at the kitchen fire, and the gate stayed shut through the winter.

choices.label: Tie it with rope
choices.chronicle: {When}, the gate was tied with rope, and it banged all winter long.

title: The Young Voice
text: A young brother's singing at Vespers has moved the old ones to tears.

choices.label: Let him sing at every feast
choices.chronicle: {When}, the young brother was given the Vespers hymn at every feast, and the old ones said it was like hearing the first brothers again.

choices.label: Ask him to sing more softly
choices.chronicle: {When}, the young brother was asked to sing more softly, and he did, and the old ones were sorry for it.

title: Charcoal Burners from the Bog
text: Charcoal burners from the bog ask for leave to cut in the house's wood.

choices.label: Let them cut a little
choices.chronicle: {When}, the burners cut a little and left a sack of charcoal at the gate, which the kitchen was glad of.

choices.label: Refuse them
choices.chronicle: {When}, the burners were refused, and went back to the bog, and the wood was left to the house.

title: A Hard Calving
text: A cow is calving badly in the byre, and the brother who knows cattle is ill in bed.

choices.label: Call the old shepherd from the village
choices.chronicle: {When}, the old shepherd came up from the village in the dark and turned the calf, and cow and calf both lived.

choices.label: Do it ourselves
choices.chronicle: {When}, the brothers did it themselves, badly; the calf lived and the cow did not, and the meat was salted down.

title: The Night Watch
text: A brother has taken a fever and asks to keep the night watch as penance.

choices.label: Let him keep the watch
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} kept the night watch through the fever, and came out of it with a cough that did not leave him.

choices.label: Send him to bed
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was sent to bed, and the night watch was shared out among the others.
